text: by: §1 . Appendix A Implementations A.1 Hardware and Software Configuration Table 1 summarizes the hardware and software configurations of the two clusters used in our evaluation. Both clusters contain four nodes with eight GPUs per node. Unless otherwise specified, the software versions correspond to the real-routing replay experiments. Table 1: Hardware and software configurations of the evaluation clusters. Configuration H800 Cluster H20 Cluster Number of nodes 4 4 GPUs per node 8 8 GPU model NVIDIA H800 NVIDIA H20 GPU memory 81,559 MiB 97,871 MiB Intra-node interconnect NVLink NVLink Number of NICs per node 8 RDMA HCA 4 RDMA HCA NIC bandwidth 200 Gb/s per port 200 Gb/s per port Inter-node network RDMA; physical fabric type not recorded RDMA; physical fabric type not recorded NVIDIA driver 550.90.07 590.48.01 CUDA 12.9 12.8 NCCL 2.30.7 2.31.2 DeepEP Official upstream base, package v2.1.0 Official upstream base, package v2.1.0 GPU–NIC mapping One PIX-proximate HCA per GPU NCCL-managed RDMA backend NCCL GIN, RAIL connection NCCL GIN, RAIL connection DeepEP communication contexts 129 GIN contexts 129 GIN contexts Communication SMs 16 16 Each H800 node has eight 400-Gb/s NVIDIA ConnectX-7 adapters, with one PIX-proximate adapter per GPU. Each H20 node has four 400-Gb/s NVIDIA ConnectX-7 adapters, each configured with two 200-Gb/s ports. Each pair of PCIe-local GPUs shares one adapter, with a separate port assigned to each GPU for port-level traffic isolation. Native, Rail-only, Permutation-only, and Joint use the same backend, based on the official DeepEP package version 2.1.0, and the same launch-level communication configuration within each paired replay experiment. The DeepEP configuration allocates 129 GIN communication contexts and uses 16 communication SMs with automatic QP selection. External baselines such as NCCL and FAST retain their own communication backends and library-specific settings. A.2 Integration with UltraEP We further evaluate RailWave when integrated with UltraEP.
